_what_this_is: One place that says which bank is which. Our paperwork calls the same bank six different names - AMEX, BK OF AMER, CAP ONE NA, Wells. This file turns every one of those spellings into a single proper name, so the computer stops treating them as six different banks.
_why_it_matters: The funding advisor's bank list is sorted by which credit bureau each bank checks, so a client does not burn three checks at the same bureau. That sorting only works if the computer knows AMEX and American Express are one bank. Today it does not, so the list comes out in alphabetical order and the plan does nothing.
_owner_rule: Chris, 2026-09-05: use the full name, never the short one. 'American Express', never 'Amex'. 'Wells Fargo', never 'Wells'.
_never_guess: If a name could be two different banks, it is listed under unresolved below and left alone. A wrong bank name sends a client's application to the exact credit bureau they were trying to protect.

how_to_use.step_1: Clean the name the same way every time. Make it lowercase. Turn a curly apostrophe into a straight one. Turn & into the word and. Replace anything that is not a letter, number, apostrophe or space with a space. Squash repeated spaces. Trim the ends.
how_to_use.step_2: Look the cleaned name up in `lookup`. What comes back is the proper name of the bank.
how_to_use.step_3: If it is not in `lookup`, stop. Leave it blank and count it as unknown. Do not fuzzy-match and do not guess.
how_to_use.warning: Never match on part of a name. 'Prosper' is inside 'Prosperity Bank' and they are two completely different companies. 'Citi' is inside 'Citizens Bank', 'Citywide Banks' and 'City National Bank'. Whole cleaned name only.

deliberately_unmapped.cbna: Bare CBNA is Citibank's issuing code AND the code on the store cards Citi issues for other brands - MACYS/CBNA, THD/CBNA, CBNA/BBY, EXXON/CBNA, OFFICEDEPOT/CBNA. Measured 2026-09-05: mapping it to Citi pulled 75 of Citi's 86 inquiry rows from store cards, which pushed Experian to 30.2% and put EX/EQ on Citi. Strip them and Citi reads 9 of 11 Equifax. A store card is not the bank's business card and must not vote on which bureau that bank pulls. Spellings that name Citi outright - CITI CARDS CBNA, CITICARDS CBNA, CITIBANK NA - stay mapped.
deliberately_unmapped.citi cards cbna / citicards cbna: Every CBNA-suffixed spelling is contaminated by the store cards Citi issues for other brands. Measured 2026-09-05: with them mapped Citi read EX/EQ, and with only the bare code removed it read EX. The 11 rows that name Citibank outright read 9 Equifax, 1 Experian, 1 TransUnion. Rather than pick a bureau by hand, all CBNA spellings are unmapped so Citi is decided only by rows that actually say Citibank.
